newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Andean Pact undecided on its re-entry.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Andean Pact undecided on its re-entry.

text.p: Representatives of the Andean Pact failed on Tuesday to reach a decision over accepting Peru back into the regional trade group, Peruvian Industry Minister Gustavo Caillaux said.
At a special closed-door meeting of the group in Lima, Caillaux presented Peru's plan for adhering to the group's common import tariff, part of his country's proposal for rejoining the bloc.
Peru applied for a gradual return to the group over eight years, pact sources said.
The pact's members -- Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela -- agreed to defer a decision on Peru's re-entry until next week, Caillaux said.
Peru decided in 1992 to temporarily leave the pact over disagreement with its tariff policy after deciding the tariff went against its internal free-market economic policies.
